clue.text: Exceptional horse with a place in the firmament

definitions.meaning: the winged horse of Greek myth, a horse like no other
a constellation of the northern sky named after that winged horse

explanation.surface: Praise for a superb racehorse that has earned a place among the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical winged steed of Greek legend also names a large constellation, so both halves fit.

clue.text: Ceremony in public building attended by politician

indicators.note: the building is accompanied by the politician, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: PO, the post office, is a public building
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A state occasion at a civic building with an MP in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour, a synonym for ceremony.

clue.text: Cellular networks criminals may have trouble setting up

parts.note: a gang is a band of criminals

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means the word is raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Mobile phone networks that crooks find hard to establish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns AIL into LIA in this down clue; 'Cellular networks' sounds like mobile phones but means masses of nerve cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganglia are clusters of nerve cells forming networks in the body, hence cellular networks.

clue.text: Rogue's fraudulent scheme to gain power

parts.note: a scam is a swindle
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A con man's swindle designed to win him influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, a mild synonym for rogue.

clue.text: Police vehicle responsible for injury going round square

indicators.note: the first word's letters surround the second word's

parts.note: a scar is the mark of an injury, here standing for it
a quad is a quadrangle, a square courtyard

explanation.surface: A patrol car that caused an accident while circling a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' is only a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad car is a police patrol car.

clue.text: One of the Bondi stars to emerge?

definitions.meaning: an expert wave-rider, a star of the breakers at Bondi, the famous Sydney beach
to come up to the top of the water

explanation.surface: A celebrated Bondi beach surfer coming up out of the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as SURF ACE, an ace of the surf; Bondi is Sydney's best-known surfing beach.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to rise into view, a direct synonym of emerge.

clue.text: In spring the girl's one to climb mountains maybe

indicators.note: the girl's word sits within the spring's word

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
her, belonging to the girl

explanation.surface: A young woman at a spa town who goes up mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as mountain guides and porters, so one who climbs mountains.

clue.text: Jane's husband eventually found in port

definitions.meaning: Jane Eyre finally marries Mr Edward, master of Thornfield, in Charlotte Bronte's novel
a Medway town in Kent with a historic dockyard and harbour

explanation.surface: Jane finally finds her future husband in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eventually' is fair because Jane Eyre only marries him at the end of the novel; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Rochester is the man Jane Eyre marries, and Rochester is a Kentish port on the Medway.

clue.text: Transport organisation's very fine leader defecting

indicators.note: the first letter deserts its word and leaves it

parts.note: a hairline crack or margin is a very fine one

explanation.surface: A carrier company whose chief has gone over to a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader defecting' drops the H at the front of HAIRLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company that transports passengers by air.

clue.text: Art of horsemanship? It lies in balance between two parts

indicators.note: the little word is placed inside the longer one

parts.note: an equation balances its two sides

explanation.surface: Asks whether riding skill is all a matter of balancing body halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Equitation is the formal term for riding and horsemanship.

clue.text: Little home, one covered in blossom

indicators.note: the home and one pieces are wrapped by the blossom word

parts.note: to blossom is to develop fully, to mature
to be in is to be at home
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A small cottage buried under flowering plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blossom' is a verb here: to mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniature as an adjective means very small, a synonym of little.

clue.text: Gosh, endless enjoyment, is provided by holiday venue!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at the non-stop fun of a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek island is a popular resort, a holiday destination.

clue.text: Editor tipples, getting drunk — one with commas to check?

indicators.note: a drunk person is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tippling editor still tries to check the punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is a butterfly, not a punctuation mark, so the checker studies butterflies.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly collector examines species such as the comma butterfly, so this is a witty description of one.

clue.text: Various lines in shop with cash register not moving at all

parts.note: stocks are the ranges of goods a shop carries
a till

explanation.surface: Merchandise in a store beside a till that never moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, standing without moving at all.

clue.text: Yob's meal uncooked always

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain
raw food is uncooked
ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A lout's dinner is always served raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yob's' means Yob is; AY for always is old and poetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearaway is a reckless young troublemaker, much like a yob.

clue.text: A lord almost without purpose has been given a role

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, a lord
the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: A noble with nothing to do finds himself given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside; 'almost' drops the last letter of the lord's title.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is someone who has been given a post; the definition describes such a person.

clue.text: Provide evidence of watching cricket?

definitions.meaning: to bear witness to or confirm
present at a test match, read as two words

explanation.surface: A witness explains they were at the cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it as AT TEST: a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or provide proof of something.

clue.text: Little devil, gadabout — one starting to get better?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous small devil
a rover wanders about

explanation.surface: A mischievous wanderer who has begun to mend his ways.
explanation.definitionFit: An improver is someone who makes things better, or a beginner learning a trade.

clue.text: In church there's a certain disrespect for religious leader

indicators.note: the inner pieces go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: lip is cheeky impertinence, one kind of disrespect

explanation.surface: Some insolence is shown in church towards a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the chief civil and religious ruler in Islam, a religious leader.

clue.text: Top people featured in newspaper articles

definitions.meaning: those at the head, in charge
editorials, the main opinion columns of a paper

explanation.surface: Prominent figures appear in press reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are those in charge, and in British papers leaders are editorial articles.

clue.text: Cupid sorts out matter involving love repeatedly

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new arrangement
repeatedly means done more than once, so the love letter appears again, giving two of it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Cupid settles a matter of love again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER plus OO, from 'love repeatedly', are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a small cupid figure in Italian art.

clue.text: A motor crashed outside English cafe

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the other letter
a crashed motor is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A car smashes into the front of an English cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns A MOTOR into TAROOM, and 'outside' puts that around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small cafe serving tea and light meals.

clue.text: Hot drink permitted in holiday accommodation

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Tea is allowed in a holiday cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin let as holiday lodging.

clue.text: Fleet in range is facing ruin centre visible in radar

parts.note: a span is a range or extent
to harm is to damage or ruin

indicators.note: only the inner letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A fleet within range faces destruction, as the radar shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre visible in' keeps ADA from RADAR; 'facing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was the fleet sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: Courts wanting a legal procedure curtailed

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a trial is a legal hearing

explanation.surface: Law courts struggle without a full trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' suggests law courts but means courtyards; 'curtailed' cuts TRIAL to TRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courts or halls in a building, plural of atrium.

clue.text: Little flowering plant makes one happy

definitions.meaning: short for gladiolus, a tall flowering plant

explanation.surface: A small flower cheers someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the shortened name, not a small plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad is short for gladiolus and also means pleased.

clue.text: That is holding wide structure together

indicators.note: the phrase contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a broad framework from falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'together' is a link; the run straddles 'wide' and 'structure'.
explanation.definitionFit: Id est is the Latin phrase meaning that is, abbreviated i.e.

clue.text: Organ fund — for one of its two cathedrals?

parts.note: the liver is a body organ
a pool is a shared fund

explanation.surface: An organ appeal to raise money for a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the city famed for having two cathedrals, one Anglican and one Catholic; 'Organ' looks musical but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: This Merseyside city has two cathedrals, so it is the place either cathedral belongs to.

clue.text: Most fleshy female consumed by desire

indicators.note: the woman's word is swallowed inside the desire word

parts.note: lust is strong desire
she, a female

explanation.surface: A voluptuous woman overwhelmed by passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lushest means most luxuriant or succulent, so most fleshy.

clue.text: Back to sea with new weapons

parts.note: rear means back
Med, short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A navy returns to sea armed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmed means supplied again with arms, so equipped with new weapons.
